name: Australian Sparkling Ale
description: Bottle-conditioned, cloudy when roused, and unchanged since the nineteenth century. Australia's one genuinely native beer style, and it predates the country's federation.
funFact: Coopers has bottle-conditioned it continuously since 1862, and the correct service is to roll the bottle gently before pouring so the yeast sediment goes into the glass rather than staying behind.

serve.how: Roll the bottle on its side — never shake it — to lift the yeast off the bottom, then pour the whole thing in one go so the sediment carries through. Expect a cloudy, lively pour with a persistent head. Serve it cool rather than cold; the pear and apple esters that define the style disappear at lager temperatures.

composition.summary: A bottle-conditioned pale ale with a distinctive fruity house yeast character.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Pale malt, kept simple so the yeast leads.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: Pride of Ringwood, an Australian hop with a firm, resinous bitterness.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: A century-old house ale strain giving pear and apple esters.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Live yeast left in the bottle for secondary conditioning.

composition.process: Warm-fermented with a heritage house strain, then bottled with live yeast to condition naturally rather than being filtered and force-carbonated.

name: New Zealand Pilsner
description: A pilsner rebuilt on New Zealand hops: gooseberry, lime leaf and passionfruit over a clean lager base. Tastes tropical without a drop of fruit in it.
funFact: Nelson Sauvin is named for its resemblance to Sauvignon Blanc, and it is the hop that made this style possible — New Zealand's hop varieties are bred in isolation, giving aromas found nowhere in the European stock.

serve.how: Serve chilled but not ice-cold, in a glass with some taper to gather the aroma — the hop character is the whole point and a straight tumbler throws it away. Pour to a firm head. Drink it fresh; New Zealand hop aromatics fade faster than European ones, and a year-old bottle is a different and lesser beer.

composition.summary: A clean lager base carrying intensely aromatic New Zealand hop varieties.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: Nelson Sauvin, Motueka and Riwaka, late and generous.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Lager yeast fermented cold for a clean backdrop.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Nothing — the hops carry the entire identity.

composition.process: Cold lager fermentation with heavy late and whirlpool hopping, lagered briefly so the aromatics survive.
